name: Mr. Jones Cranefly
imitates: An adult cranefly that skates, skips and hops on the surface; tied for hot afternoons and early mornings when the naturals are active.
recipe: 6/0 tan Uni-Thread and 18/0 Semperfli Nano Silk

steps.text: Mount a fine sewing needle in the vise, wax it, wrap a thread base and tie McFlylon on top of the needle, then wrap back to a stopping point.
Cut a 2mm foam sliver, tie it on top of the needle about a third of the way along and wrap it back to the stopping point.
Add a mono loop at the front of the extended abdomen, glue the underbody, then wrap the foam strip forward in overlapping turns with a taper at the front. Tie off and whip finish.
Twist the body off the needle, then pull the tag thread out the back to cinch the underbody. Trim the tag and yarn flush.
In a Tiemco 2487, tie a stacked bunch of bleached moose hair behind the eye as the forward wing, matched to the abdomen length.
Tie the extended body on by its mono stub, fold the mono into a loop and bind it down. Dub a small ball and tie in barred Flex-Floss legs on each side of it.
Bind a wider strip of foam along the top of the shank, glue the tie-down area and dub a ball-shaped thorax.
Tie in a second matched clump of moose hair on top between the thorax and the forward wing.
Split that clump into two side wings, draw the foam strip forward between them and tie it down gently to form the wingcase.
Prop the forward wing up with a small thread head, whip finish, color the body, legs and thorax with markers, trim the legs and fan the wings flat.
